title: Localization Hom and multiplication tower criterion
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site with small underlying category, let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, let $f\in\mathcal O(U)$, and let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the slice site $\mathcal C/U$, let $T(K|_U,f)$ be a derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit] in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ of the tower $\cdots\xrightarrow{f}K|_U\xrightarrow{f}K|_U$ whose transition maps are multiplication by $f$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Then $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],K|_U)=0$ if and only if $T(K|_U,f)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af), especially the equivalence of (1) and (3) via the free resolution of $\mathcal O_f$ and the derived multiplication tower.

proof.text: Work on the small slice ringed site $\mathcal S=\mathcal C/U$, with ring $\mathcal O_U$ and $L=K|_U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Its objects are arrows of the small category $\mathcal C$ with target $U$, and its morphisms are commuting triangles in $\mathcal C$, so the slice is small. Choose a complex representing $L$ and a K-injective resolution $I^\bullet$ with every $I^n$ injective, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on $\mathcal S$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], for any module sheaf $A$ placed in degree zero, $R\mathcal Hom(A,L)$ is represented by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A[0],I^\bullet)$. We choose the replacement on the slice itself, so no preservation of injectivity under restriction is presumed.

Put $P=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal O_U$. The exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{d}P\to\mathcal O_U[1/f]\to0$ of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-free-resolution], viewed as a degree-zero short exact sequence of complexes, gives the distinguished triangle $P\xrightarrow{d}P\to\mathcal O_U[1/f]\to P[1]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Apply the contravariant triangulated functor $R\mathcal Hom(-,L)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and rotate to obtain $R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/f],L)\to R\mathcal Hom(P,L)\xrightarrow{d^*}R\mathcal Hom(P,L)\to R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/f],L)[1]$. The middle arrow is precomposition by $d$. This uses derived internal-Hom exactness, without assuming that an arbitrary K-injective complex has injective terms or that products of sheaves are exact.

Compute the two middle objects using the representative $I^\bullet$ of Step 1. The definitions [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-hom-complex] identify $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[0],I^\bullet)$ with $\prod_{n\ge0}I^\bullet$: locally, a map out of the free sum is determined by the images $x_n$ of its basis generators, and any such family defines a map by $\sum a_ne_n\mapsto\sum a_nx_n$ on finite-support representatives and then by gluing. The differential is coordinatewise $d_I$ because $P[0]$ has zero differential. Since $d(e_n)=e_n-fe_{n+1}$ in the resolution, precomposition sends $(x_n)_n$ to $(x_n-fx_{n+1})_n$. This also identifies the projection to each factor with restriction to its basis summand.

Products in module sheaves exist and are sectionwise [def-pur-hom-complex]. Apply [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective] with the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$ and the set $\mathbf N$, taking every complex to be $I^\bullet$. Thus $\prod_n I^\bullet$, with its coordinate projections, represents $\prod_n L$ in the derived category, without an exact-countable-products hypothesis. Under these projections the middle morphism in Step 2 has coordinate $\mathrm{pr}_n-f\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ by Step 3, hence it is precisely $1-s$ for the multiplication tower [def-weil-derived-limit]. Reindex the factors by $m=n+1$ to use the $m\geq1$ convention of that definition; the coordinate formula becomes $\mathrm{pr}_m-f\mathrm{pr}_{m+1}$ with the identical transition maps. The triangle in Step 2 therefore exhibits $R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/f],L)$ as a derived limit of that tower.

The object $T(L,f)$ in the statement is any derived limit of the same tower. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] gives an isomorphism between it and the derived limit exhibited in Step 4. An object is isomorphic to zero if and only if any isomorphic object is isomorphic to zero. Consequently $R\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O_U[1/f],L)=0$ if and only if $T(L,f)=0$. No canonical choice of derived limit is needed.
